analysis:
The two units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, lines 2126-2612, which is documentation. They show the pre-change release history. The patch excerpt shows the head only adds a new v0.10.8 candidate section at the top and is truncated, so I could not review the rest of the added text. The changed ranges are documentation only, and no executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling logic is touched.

The base text I examined has no new attack surface. Several entries bear on retained threats and are unchanged by this PR: T-041 (the SSD prefix cache, 30-minute TTL and the 4 TB write budget), the TB-011 App Attest behavior, TB-003 and the T-043 watchdog, TB-010 and the fan helper, and the staging and dev release lanes. The dev-lane installer relaxation is a documented pre-existing decision for -dev. and -staging. versions only. It does not touch production.

I did not see the full head text of the new v0.10.8 section, so claims it makes cannot be checked against code here. A later pass should check that the changelog does not misstate security posture, such as the cluster pairing and update behavior. The visible patch says a pair running different builds fails closed, and the pair update installs on both Macs or neither. Cluster pairing, the update flow and the coordinator pair-approval limits are outside the supplied evidence and may need threat-model coverage if they introduce a new trust boundary. Without the head text or the code, I make no claim either way, and I record that as a coverage limit rather than as evidence of safety.
